newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Kingsteam to merge with An Feng Steel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Kingsteam to merge with An Feng Steel.

text.p: Kingstream Resources NL said on Friday it planned to merge with An Feng Steel Co Ltd, its Taiwan-based partner in the proposed A$1.4 billion Midwest Iron and Steel project in Western Australia.
In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX), Kingsteam said it had exchanged letters of intent with An Feng and had secured conditional support from An Feng's principal shareholders.
Kingsteam said the merged company would be based in Perth and would have assets in excess of A$1 billion.

"The merger will create a fully integrated steel enterprise, capturing and marrying the economic benefits of available gas, power and iron ore in Western Australia and the rapidly expanding markets for steel products in Asia," the company said.

Kingstream will issue 615 million shares to An Feng shareholders at an issue price based on the final assessed valuation of the An Feng and Kingstream assets. The company will then acquire all of 499 million issued shares in An Feng.
An Feng shareholders will also receive 6.3 million five year options exercisable at A$1.10 each and, subject to the merger's completion, 35.8 million options on the same terms.
Current Kingstream shareholders will hold about a 17.4 percent interest in the merged group with An Feng shareholders holding the balance of 82.6 percent.

Kingstream said the exact number of new shares and options to be issued would depend on the rounding of individual entitlements and the exercise of existing Kingstream options to participate in the entitlement.
Under the proposal, the existing 14.29 million Kingstream shares owned by An Feng would be cancelled.
Kingstream and An Feng Steel signed a heads of agreement in May to develop the Midwest Iron and Steel project, which is expected to produce 2.4 million tonnes of steel slab a year.
The May agreement provided for An Feng to contribute 70 percent of equity and Kingstream 30 percent.

Kingstream said the merger was subject to a number of conditions and regulatory approvals. It said it was endeavouring to satisfy all conditions and to seek all necessary approvals by March 31 this year.
"Kingstream will immediately proceed with the due diligence process and with the appointment of an appropriate independent expert to report on the transaction," the company said.

The merger is also subject to An Feng and Kingstream shareholder approval and various government and regulatory approvals including Republic of China foreign investment approval and Australian Foreign Investment Review Board approval.
Kingstream shares closed at 95 cents on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of A$63.49 million based on its 668.26 million shares outstanding.
